evals.name: cached-scope-question
evals.prompt: I'm calling SCAPI Shopper Products getProducts from a headless storefront. What OAuth scopes do I need on my shopper token? The scraped JSON is already at /tmp/dsc-query-eval/cache/ -- you don't need to scrape, just look it up and answer.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs dsc-query's query.js against the pre-seeded cache, extracts the security[] field, and reports the scopes 'sfcc.shopper-products' and 'sfcc.shopper-standard' via the ShopperToken scheme. Answer includes the file path so the user can verify. Does not scrape, does not dump the entire endpoint JSON.
expectations: Agent's final answer names both scopes: sfcc.shopper-products AND sfcc.shopper-standard
Agent's final answer names the security scheme: ShopperToken
Agent did not run dsc-scrape (or any HTTP fetch) for this question -- the cache was pre-seeded
Agent cited the file path to the endpoint JSON so the user can verify
Agent did not paste the full endpoint JSON into the answer (too verbose)

evals.name: cache-miss-auto-scrape
evals.prompt: For SCAPI shopper-baskets, what's the request body shape for createBasket? Use /tmp/dsc-query-eval/cache/ as the cache dir. Scrape if you need to.
evals.expected_output: Agent checks the cache, sees shopper-baskets is not present (exit 2 from query.js), runs dsc-scrape with the reference-root URL (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/shopper-baskets) into the same cache dir, then retries query.js --field body --resolve-refs and reports the Basket request body shape -- should include productItems, giftCertificateItems, shipments, etc. Does NOT WebFetch the page manually, does NOT scrape a single slug first, does NOT leave the answer at '$ref: Basket' without inlining.
expectations: Agent invoked dsc-scrape's scrape.js (by file path, not via the Skill tool) with a /references/shopper-baskets URL
Agent scraped the reference root (no ?meta= in the URL), not a single slug
Agent's final answer describes concrete Basket fields (at least 3 of: productItems, giftCertificateItems, shipments, billingAddress, customerInfo, couponItems, currency), not just 'returns a Basket'
Agent cited the file path to the endpoint JSON for verification
Agent did not attempt to WebFetch or curl the DSC page as a substitute for scraping

evals.name: response-schema-with-ref-resolution
evals.prompt: What does shopper-products getProduct actually return on a 200 response? Give me the real fields, not just a type name. Cache is at /tmp/dsc-query-eval/cache/ and shopper-products is already scraped.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs query.js with --field responses --resolve-refs (or equivalently reads getProduct.json's responses[] and then reads types/Product.json to inline the schema). Answer describes actual fields -- at minimum id, name, price, currency -- not just 'returns a Product'. Does NOT leave the user with '$ref: #/components/schemas/Product' as the answer.
expectations: Agent's answer describes concrete fields from the Product type (at least 3 real field names like id, name, price, currency, imageGroups, inventory, etc.), not just the type name
Agent did not leave the response described as '$ref: #/components/schemas/Product' or similar unresolved
Agent cited the file path(s) used (either getProduct.json plus types/Product.json, or mentioned both)
Agent did not WebFetch the DSC page to get the schema -- the cache is pre-seeded

evals.name: ambiguous-slug-disambiguate
evals.prompt: In shopper-products, what parameters does the category endpoint take? The cache is at /tmp/dsc-query-eval/cache/ and shopper-products is already scraped.
evals.expected_output: The user said 'the category endpoint' which is ambiguous -- shopper-products has both getCategory (single) and getCategories (plural/list). Agent should disambiguate: either list both candidates and ask, or present both answers. Does NOT silently pick one and pretend the question was unambiguous. Once resolved, the agent describes the parameters (path/query) for whichever endpoint is confirmed.
expectations: Agent recognized the ambiguity between getCategory and getCategories (named both somewhere in the response)
Agent either (a) asked the user to pick, or (b) described both endpoints' parameters -- did not silently choose one without calling out the ambiguity
Agent's response includes parameter details (at minimum categoryId for getCategory or ids for getCategories, plus siteId)
Agent cited the file path(s) to the endpoint JSON
